3. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant states that he prima-facie has a good case on merits and there is every likelihood that the appellant would succeed in the present appeal.
It is further stated that the appellant belongs to poor strata of society, who was working as a daily wager and was living with wife and one son.

It is further stated that the appellant has already S. Alam vs The State on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39495526/

sentences.text: Therefore, it is prayed that the sentence awarded to him in the present case may be suspended during the pendency of the present appeal.
4. The learned APP appearing on behalf of the State, on the other hand, argues that the nature of offence is serious as the appellant has been convicted under the POCSO Act.
The victim in this case is aged about 10 years.
It is therefore submitted that the present application be rejected.

5. In light of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, and the fact that the disposal of the appeal is likely to take sometime and the appellant is the only bread earner of his family, the present application is allowed.

It is directed that the sentence awarded to the appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of the present petition, subject to his furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs. 10,000/- with one surety bond of the like amount, subject to satisfaction of the learned Trial Court/Successor Court/Link Court/Duty Judge, on the following terms and conditions:
i) The appellant shall not leave the country without prior permission of the concerned Court.
ii) In case of change of residential address/contact
